11.0.0.en: Christ was praying because He is a perfect man who needs prayer, just as He is perfect God, and He is also the representative of mankind who offers prayer on our behalf so that our prayers may be sanctified in Him, and so that He may give us a model to imitate in our spiritual life.

11.0.1.en: The disciples noticed the fervor of Christ's prayer, and wished that He would teach them this fervent prayer, especially since spiritual leaders such as John the Baptist and the Pharisees taught their disciples particular prayers.

11.0.2.en: And this disciple who asked Christ was expressing the feelings of all the disciples, for he said, Teach us how to pray.

11.1.0.en: In order to approach prayer, we must enter in the spirit of sonship to God as a heavenly Father, so that we in turn are heavenly in our thoughts and conduct, and our sonship gives us boldness and confidence in prayer that God answers us and cares about our words.

11.1.1.en: The Lord's Prayer is the example that we follow in all our private prayers, in addition to our repeating it because of the depth of the meanings it contains.

11.1.2.en: The Lord's Prayer includes two parts, the first being the glorifying of God mentioned in this verse, and the second the requests for ourselves mentioned in the following two verses, so that we learn to glorify God first before we ask for anything. The name of God has been holy from eternity, but our asking that His name be hallowed means its being sanctified in us in our words and good works.

11.1.3.en: Then we ask that God reign over our hearts, so that we come out of the bondage of sin and the lusts of the world. It is a prayer that expresses our longings to obey God and submit to Him, and even our longings for the eternal Kingdom.

11.1.4.en: Then, as we look at God's ordering in heaven and the obedience of the angels to Him, we long to surrender our lives to Him, so that His will leads us and not our own purposes, which are liable to error. The will of God in heaven and on earth also means in the spirit and in the body.

11.2.0.en: The daily bread means Christ, whether His most holy Body and Blood, or His life-giving word, because Christ is the bread that came down from heaven as He said in (Jn 6:58). And in other translations such as the Coptic it says our bread that is coming, or of tomorrow, or essential, all of which mean that Christ is our spiritual bread.

11.2.1.en: The daily bread also means that we ask God for our material needs day by day, because we rely on Him in all our affairs, so we are in need of Him and do not think that we are self-sufficient by our own ability.

11.2.2.en: This does not mean that we are absorbed in material requests, but our need of the necessities, that is, bread, because we are in the body, and that we are not preoccupied with the future and its needs, which trouble our thoughts.

11.3.0.en: We confess our sins that God may forgive them, whose power to forgive we trust, and we cannot obtain this forgiveness for our sins, which are great because they are directed against God, unless we first forgive others their sins against us, which are small because they are between human beings. The meaning of this is that unforgiveness deprives us of the forgiveness of our sins. Then, feeling our weakness, we ask God not to allow us trials, but this humility does not mean rejecting God's will if He wants to test us with a trial that benefits us spiritually; therefore we say to Him, if You allow us a trial, deliver us from the evil devil who wants to make us fall into sin and take us away from You.

11.3.1.en: I wish you would pray the Lord's Prayer calmly so that you grasp its meanings, and so submit to God and enjoy fellowship with Him, and love everyone and live in assurance.

11.4.0.en: Christ gave a parable on the importance of importunity in prayer, not because He does not know our needs or because repetition in itself is useful, but because it shows the faith of the one praying and his clinging to God, and his declaring his weakness and need, so that he receives God's mercies which He wants to pour out upon him.

11.4.1.en: The parable tells the story of a man to whom a guest came at midnight, that is, at a critical time, and he did not have the necessary food to feed him, so he went to his neighbor and friend, knocking at his door and asking him for food.

11.4.2.en: Midnight: a symbol of the time of affliction that a person passes through, so that he has recourse to others to help him, and he asks on behalf of a guest who has come to him from a journey, that is, he prays to God for the needs of others, to rescue these sinners or those in distress.

11.4.3.en: The three loaves symbolize the necessary food, which is faith in the Holy Trinity, and they symbolize also faith, hope and love, and likewise the need of the spirit, the soul and the body.

11.5.0.en: The friend answered from within, declaring that the time was not suitable for answering his request, since he was asleep with his children. This sleeper is selfish, thinking of his own comfort, and does not want to help his neighbor whatever his need. Our Christ did not love us from within heaven but became incarnate and came to us, and He is always awake and never sleeps, and His angels (His children) also are attentive, always praising Him and interceding for us, and the door is no longer shut through Christ's Incarnation and redemption, for His resurrection from the dead satisfies all our needs.

11.6.0.en: The friend within refused at first to answer his friend's request, but as a result of the importunity he rose and gave him what he asked. If the selfish, lazy sleeper moved because of importunity and gave to his neighbor, how much more God who is love, who rejoices in the importunity of His children in prayer and gives them their needs.

11.7.0.en: Something like this passage (vv. 9-13) is mentioned in (Mt 7:7-11), and Christ said it at another time than this occasion.

11.7.1.en: Our God, who is love, urges us to ask of Him and to persist, so that He may pour out His gifts upon us, for He wants to give and we do not want to ask, and His slowness in answering our requests is not neglect of us but a testing of our love and our clinging to Him. The threefold repetition of the asking is that it may be of thought, word and deed, that is, we think of God, and raise our voices in prayer and with it our hands also, and we prostrate many times beseeching Him, and it is noticed that the request increases until it reaches knocking with the hands vehemently because of the greatness of the need.

11.8.0.en: Christ gives another example of the answering of prayer, which is a son asking his father for bread, and it is expected that he will give it to him, and it is not reasonable that he would give him a stone instead of bread, because the tenderness of fatherhood refuses that.

11.8.1.en: The same applies if the son asks for a fish: he will not give him a serpent that harms him instead of the food he asked for, or if he asks for an egg, it is unreasonable that he would give him instead of it a scorpion that kills him with its poison.

11.8.2.en: Bread: a symbol of love, because it is the father's gift to his children that they may live.

11.8.3.en: The stone: points to hardness of heart, that is, lack of love.

11.8.4.en: The fish: a symbol of faith, since it swims out of sight within the water.

11.8.5.en: The egg: a symbol of hope, since despite its small size we hope that a bird will come out of it that moves and flies, and God cannot give us, instead of hope, what drives us away from Him and frightens us.

11.8.6.en: So the three requests symbolize the request for faith, hope and love, and show that fatherhood necessarily requires caring for the children's requests and fulfilling them.

11.9.0.en: Christ draws a proof from this parable, that fleshly fathers understand how to give good gifts to their children because they love them, how much more God the heavenly Father, the source of all fatherhood and tenderness, who gives to His children who ask of Him not only the material gifts they ask for, but rather the work of His Holy Spirit in them, to establish their faith, their love and their hope in Him, so that they believe that He answers their material requests by His fatherly tenderness, and likewise comforts their hearts and supports them throughout their lives.

11.9.1.en: The tender God wants to give you many of the treasures of His love, so ask of Him with a faith that shows your perseverance and your importunity toward Him with the boldness of sonship, however hard the request, and even if God delays in answering, do not despair but rely on Him, because He cares for you until He answers your request. And if His will is something other than what you ask, He will give you rest and joy in His better divine ordering of your life.

11.10.s.en: (3) The accusation of Christ with Beelzebub

11.10.0.en: A devil dwelt in a man and deprived him of the ability to speak, and Christ cast him out of him and he spoke again, and the crowds were amazed at the greatness of the miracle, even including the scribes and Pharisees who oppose Christ.

11.10.1.en: Sin deprives you of the ability to speak the word of God, and by repentance you regain good speech.

11.11.0.en: Beelzebub: the Aramaic pronunciation of Beelzebul, the god of the Ekronites, and it means lord of the flies, that is, the one who drives away flies.

11.11.1.en: Those who resisted Christ could not deny the miracle, and because they did not want to believe in Him and hardened their hearts, they accused Him of dealing with Beelzebub the prince of the devils so as to be able to cast out devils, and that this was not authority of His over Satan, but that by the authority of Satan He casts out devils.

11.12.0.en: Another group of those who resisted, who refused to believe despite the greatness of the miracle, asked for a new miracle in order to believe, and of course they would not be able to, because the spirit of doubt was within them, and therefore Christ did not respond to them.

11.13.0.en: Christ answered their doubts by making clear a logical truth, which is that division destroys any house or kingdom, and consequently the division of Satan's kingdom would ruin it, and this is proof that Christ has authority over the demons, and that it is not the prince of the devils who casts out devils.

11.13.1.en: How dangerous is division within the home, the Church or any society; so whatever the sacrifice, let us seek unity, to keep God within us and working in us.

11.14.0.en: Completing His answer He said, if we suppose that my power is the power of the prince of the devils, then your sons, that is, His Jewish disciples whom they know, by whose authority did they cast out devils? Surely not by a relationship with the prince of the devils, but by the authority I gave them, and by their faith they judge you and expose your doubts.

11.15.0.en: The finger of God -: by it He means the hand of God and His Spirit, that is, that Christ's authority is from Himself because He is God, and this means that the Kingdom of God has come near to the Jews by the Incarnation of Christ, so that He reigns over the hearts of His believing children and judges the unbelievers who reject His reign.

11.16.s.en: (4) The parable of the strong man and the stronger

11.16.0.en: The strong man is Satan, who used to strengthen people by his evils and draw them to hell before the coming of Christ. Satan's arms are the lusts, his palace is hell, and his goods are the souls subject to him who walked in evil.

11.17.0.en: The stronger than he is Christ, who overcomes him by the Cross and takes his spoils, that is, the souls held captive in hell, and the risen Christ sets them free and brings them up to Paradise.

11.17.1.en: This is what happens when Satan makes any person fall into evil lusts, but if he has recourse by repentance to Christ, He forgives them to him and frees him from the bondage of the devil, and even establishes him in the new life by His most holy Body and Blood.

11.18.0.en: Christ here directs attention to the importance of positive action, for whoever refuses to gather souls with Christ gives Satan an opportunity to scatter them, and by this shares with him in drawing people away from God and so is against God. Do not fear the power of the devil or his threats and wars, for they are nothing before the power of God who is with you. Seek God with humility and importunity in all your afflictions, and when the devil fights you, or even after you fall into sin, He frees you and supports you and drives the devil away from you.

11.19.s.en: (5) The parable of the seven unclean spirits

11.19.0.en: Christ gave a new parable to stress the importance of positive action, saying that there is a man who has an unclean spirit, who by the grace of God was able to be rid of it, and this man became sound again, but the unclean spirit kept seeking another wicked man in whom to dwell and found no water, that is, no opportunity for life and dwelling in another person, so he thought to return to his first friend, perhaps he could find in him a readiness for evil and enter him again. This declares the activity of Satan and his constant search for opportunities to fight us, so continual watchfulness is necessary by living with God, so that he does not find a gap through which to enter our lives.

11.20.0.en: Satan found his first friend, that is, his spirit and body, empty of every good work, and adorned with an inclination to evil lusts.

11.21.0.en: Satan rejoiced greatly and found it an opportunity to cooperate with a group of devils numbering seven, that is, a great complete number, so he brought them and they dwelt in this man, and so he rushed into many evils, and his end became worse than the beginning of his life.

11.21.1.en: We ought to seize the spiritual opportunities when God removes the wars of the demons from us, even for a short time, to cling to God and grow in His love, so that if the devil tries to attack us again he finds us in greater strength and is afraid and draws away.

11.22.0.en: From the greatness of Christ's words and miracles, a woman of the crowd blessed the mother of Christ, because in Jewish society a woman is blessed through her good offspring.

11.23.0.en: Christ did not reject the blessing of His mother, but directed attention to the more important thing, which is the blessing of whoever hears and does His word, and this is a still greater blessing for the Virgin, for she not only bore Christ, but she is a spiritual person who keeps the word of God at the highest level.

11.23.1.en: The door is open for you to share with the Virgin and be blessed if you take care to read the Holy Bible and carry it out as a personal message to you every day.

11.24.0.en: Many of the Jews asked to see signs from Christ although He had done many miracles, but they still asked for other miracles, so Christ declared to them plainly that they needed the sign of Jonah the prophet, that is, his preaching of repentance to the people of Nineveh; for they needed repentance from their doubts and their pride, and seeing any miracles would not profit them without repentance.

11.25.0.en: As Jonah preached repentance to the people of Nineveh, so Christ preaches repentance to the Jews, because the Kingdom of Heaven has come near to them. And as Jonah came out of the belly of the whale alive after three days, so Christ died three days and then rose. And as Jonah gave life to the people of Nineveh through their obedience to his word, so Christ gives eternal life to those who keep His commandments.

11.26.0.en: Christ rebukes His hearers for their unbelief, although the queen of the south, that is, of Sheba (Ethiopia or Yemen), a Gentile, believed in the wisdom of Solomon, whereas the Jews have before them the hypostasis of Wisdom Himself, God the Word, and they refuse to believe in Him.

11.27.0.en: Christ makes clear the judgment awaiting His hearers if they persist in their unbelief, because the Gentile people of Nineveh, by their faith at hearing the word of Jonah, will condemn the Jews who reject the good news of Christ, who is greater than Jonah.

11.27.1.en: Do not reject the word of God sent to you in various ways, calling you to repentance, so that you may be saved on the Day of Judgment.

11.28.0.en: A candle is the word of God, which must be made known through our lives, and if we hide it those around us will not benefit from it, so we do not put it under the bushel of worldly preoccupations or human logical measurements. In a secret place: that is, hiding the teachings and not proclaiming them, because this will prevent people from benefiting from them.

11.28.1.en: A bushel is a vessel whose mouth is narrower than its base, used for measuring the quantities of grain when sold, in place of scales.

11.28.2.en: The Pharisees were accusing Christ of not declaring His teachings, and demanding signs from Him, although He was declaring His teachings and working miracles, but the problem was their unreadiness to believe, for they were placing the bushel of doubt over their hearts so that they could not believe.

11.29.0.en: The light that is in thee be darkness: that is, your eye, which was supposed to be a light to your body, into which good feelings enter that help faith, becomes on the contrary darkened by its evil, seeing only doubt and condemnation, and so keeps the heart away from faith.

11.29.1.en: Christ moves the talk from the candle to the eye, for the single eye is the light of the body. The meaning of the single eye is the one that sees God and His works in everything around it, and sees the virtues of others and thanks God for everything, and then a person is filled with peace and is lit by the light of God within him. But the evil eye, that is, the one that sees the sins of others, condemns them and murmurs, so its body is filled with disturbance and weariness.

11.29.2.en: And here Christ makes clear to the Pharisees the reason for their unbelief, which is that their eyes are evil and doubt Him, so their hearts refuse to believe in Him.

11.29.3.en: You must examine your eyes so that your looks may be single, that is, a source of rest and happiness for you, and keep away from every evil look that darkens your life and corrupts it.

11.30.0.en: Take care that your look is single, and Christ the true Lamp will shine for you with a brightness that gladdens your life always.

11.31.0.en: While Christ was teaching the crowds, one of the Pharisees invited Him to eat the midday meal with him, and Christ accepted and went in and sat down at table.

11.31.1.en: The Pharisees were a proud sect of the Jews, who felt themselves distinguished in spiritual knowledge, and represented the aristocratic class.

11.31.2.en: And although Christ knew that this Pharisee was not pure in his invitation, but wanted to catch Him in an error, yet He accepted the invitation and seized it as an opportunity to teach him and the Pharisees with him.

11.31.3.en: Be positive despite the evil of those around you. Do not fear them, and declare the truth to them for the salvation of their souls in the manner that suits them.

11.32.0.en: It was among the traditions of the Pharisees to wash before the meal, and this points to the importance of purification before any work, and it symbolizes Baptism before partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord. The Pharisees did not want to understand the prophecies about Christ, and were content to hold to the symbols, and Christ intended not to wash before eating, not because He is against external purification, but to teach the Pharisees to care for purity of heart before external purity by washing the hands before eating. And the Pharisee (between himself and his fellow Pharisees) condemned Christ because He had not washed.

11.33.0.en: It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:25-26). The Pharisees cared for outward spiritual appearances in order to obtain the praise of men, while their hearts were full of evil, so Christ rebuked them, not because washing before food is wrong, but for clinging to the appearance without the substance, and caring for men's praise of them without purifying their inner hearts.

11.33.1.en: What is meant by the platter is the dish, for it is unreasonable that the inside of the cup or the dish should be full of filth and a person eat and drink from them, content with their outward cleanness.

11.33.2.en: For God is the Creator of the outward body and the inward spirit, and indeed the inner heart is more important than the outward bodily appearance, and God asks for inward purity and then outward purity.

11.34.0.en: Christ set down a solution to the problem of the Pharisees, which is pride and selfishness, that they should come out of thinking about themselves to feeling for others, and give alms to the needy, so that their hearts are filled with love and cleansed of selfishness.

11.34.1.en: This makes clear that they need giving and love of others before caring for outward purity, for if they give alms to others their food and possessions become clean because of their love, more than by their purity because of their washing or the cleansing of their vessels on the outside.

11.35.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 23:23), a continuation of the clinging to the appearances of worship without its substance: the Pharisees were careful in their teaching of the people to give tithes of everything, even the plants of mint and rue, which is a medicinal plant, and likewise the plants of pulse, and they neglected the declaration of truth and the love of God, so Christ called them to care for the substance and then to care for the outward appearances of worship.

11.36.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 23:6). Christ also rebuked their love and pursuit of the praise of men, and their care to be glorified by them in places of worship such as the synagogues or public places such as the markets, and by this their inner pride increases.

11.37.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 23:27). Christ likened the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, who clung to outward worship while their hearts were full of pride and evil, to graves hidden under the ground whose surface looks like beautiful ground but inside are the bones of the dead; their outside appears alive with God, and their inside is death because of their distance from Him, and people glorify them and do not know the evil of their hearts. It is good that you have a sound appearance, but the more important thing is that your heart be pure in repentance and rejection of evil thoughts, so that the purity of your heart appears in your readiness for love, giving and serving those around you.

11.38.0.en: One of the lawyers present in the Pharisee's house objected to Christ's rebuke, because it was directed also to the lawyers, for they share with the Pharisees in the preceding sins.

11.38.1.en: The lawyers are those who hold to the Law and teach the statutes to the people, and most of them were Pharisees.

11.39.0.en: It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:4). Christ was not disturbed by the lawyers' objection, but seized it as an opportunity to rebuke them that they might repent, and said to them that they demand of people heavy and hard teachings and do not apply the least of them in their own personal lives. I wish you would try to carry out in your life first all that you teach others, so that your words may be strong, tried and effective in others, and your words and teachings may be for your own spiritual growth and benefit before those who hear you.

11.40.0.en: It is also mentioned in (Mt 23:29). Christ also rebuked the lawyers' care in building the tombs of the prophets and adorning them, while they did not repent of the sins of their fathers who killed the prophets and did not submit to their teachings which speak of Christ who stands among them now. By this they bear witness against themselves that they are the sons of the killers of the prophets, and were not cleansed of this trait because they did not repent and did not obey the teachings of Christ.

11.41.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 23:34-36). The wisdom of God, that is, Christ, said that He would send many prophets and apostles to call them to repentance, and if they did not repent, the blood of these prophets would bear witness to their wickedness, and all the wicked would be punished in eternal torment for the shedding of the blood of the martyrs, from the blood of Abel, the first martyr of the world, to the blood of Zacharias, who is said to be Zacharias the father of John the Baptist, whom the soldiers killed after he had placed the child John on the altar and the angel snatched him away to take him to the wilderness, so the soldiers charged with killing the children of Bethlehem under two years old were enraged and killed Zacharias.

11.42.0.en: It is mentioned in (Mt 23:3). When the lawyer reached the age of thirty they gave him a key, a sign of his authority to teach others the knowledge of God, and the aim of the Law is the knowledge of the awaited Messiah, but they did not believe in Him, and by their teachings they also prevented others from believing, that is, they used their authority wrongly, so their punishment is severe.

11.43.0.en: They urge vehemently: they become enraged and bear malice against Him, and intend to wrong Him.

11.43.1.en: Provoke him to speak: they question Him and dispute with Him, hoping to make Him fall into some error.

11.43.2.en: To catch him: that is, to seize upon any word that condemns Him.

11.43.3.en: To accuse him before the rulers of the Jews that He is a blasphemer, or before the Romans that He is a agitator of the people.

11.43.4.en: The scribes, Pharisees and lawyers were enraged because Christ exposed their errors, and instead of repenting they tried to resist His words and to catch some fault in Him so as to try Him and prevent His teachings, which show their sins. Receive the voice of God on the lips of others if it shows your faults so that you may repent, and do not be vexed with them but thank them.

11.43.5.en: Hypocrisy, fear and concern for material things. Hypocrisy (vv. 1-3):

11.43.6.en: 1- In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples "first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy. 2- For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known. 3- Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops."
